claim: Correlated timing residuals require covariance-aware fitting of both residuals and the timing design matrix.
method_notes: GLS expressed through Cholesky whitening of observations and model
limitations: Depends on an adequate covariance estimate

claim: Annual power is strongly coupled to astrometric fitting.
method_notes: Position and proper motion act through annual harmonics

claim: Empirical null maxima and injection recovery can calibrate a pulsar-planet trigger and sensitivity.
method_notes: 10000 noise-only trials and 1000 injection trials per frequency with a 90 percent recovery boundary
limitations: Nulls were white rather than release-covariance realizations

claim: Fitting the timing model can absorb an injected planet signal.
method_notes: TEMPO refitting imposed an approximately 2.5 sensitivity penalty in the authors' synthetic test
limitations: Single simulated pulsar and no red noise in that calibration

claim: Sensitivity near one year is materially degraded by fitted position proper motion and distance.
method_notes: The paper describes near-impossibility at 1 yr and a sensitivity trough

claim: Modern planet searches fit deterministic timing white noise red noise and planet parameters simultaneously.
limitations: Mostly ordinary pulsars and computationally heavier than Pilot 1

claim: A high periodic-model evidence value can still reflect quasi-periodic intrinsic behavior.
method_notes: Multiple significant periodicities were attributed to QP or magnetospheric alternatives
limitations: Pulse-profile evidence is unavailable in the current NANOGrav TOA-only pilot

claim: A dedicated one-year bin is appropriate because astrometric fitting reduces sensitivity there.
method_notes: EPTA uses a dedicated 340 to 390 day bin
limitations: Exact width is data and model dependent

claim: J1744 has significant achromatic red noise and long-period ambiguity in an independent MSP data set.
method_notes: J1744 residual comparison includes red-noise terms and planet and QP fits compete for long-timescale power
limitations: EPTA data differ from NANOGrav 15-year data

claim: Projected-mass upper limits are appropriately reported by period bin and exclude the annual sensitivity gap.
method_notes: 95 percent projected-mass limits by period bin with one-year exclusion
limitations: Bayesian posterior limits are not identical to frequentist injection completeness
